copy.original: StyleSync - Import Design Tokens & Styles into Framer
copy.value: StyleSync - Import Design Tokens & Styles into Framer

copy.original: StyleSync is a Framer plugin that extracts actively-used styles from your Figma files, design token files, and websites, and imports them directly into Framer as native color and text styles. No manual copying, no missed tokens, no mismatched values.
copy.value: StyleSync is a Framer plugin that extracts actively-used styles from your Figma files, design token files, and websites, and imports them directly into Framer as native color and text styles. No manual copying, no missed tokens, no mismatched values.

copy.original: Every design workflow involves moving styles between tools. Designers maintain color palettes and typography in Figma, developers define tokens in CSS or JSON, and production sites carry their own computed styles. Getting those values into Framer accurately and quickly is tedious work done manually.
copy.value: Every design workflow involves moving styles between tools. Designers maintain color palettes and typography in Figma, developers define tokens in CSS or JSON, and production sites carry their own computed styles. Getting those values into Framer accurately and quickly is tedious work done manually.

copy.original: StyleSync automates that transfer. It reads your styles from wherever they live, shows you a preview with full control over what gets imported, and injects only the styles you select directly into your Framer project as native color styles and text styles, accessible from any element in the canvas.
copy.value: StyleSync automates that transfer. It reads your styles from wherever they live, shows you a preview with full control over what gets imported, and injects only the styles you select directly into your Framer project as native color styles and text styles, accessible from any element in the canvas.

copy.original: StyleSync supports three distinct import methods, each designed for a different point in your workflow.
copy.value: StyleSync supports three distinct import methods, each designed for a different point in your workflow.

copy.original: Paste any Figma file URL and StyleSync scans the entire document for actively-used styles. Rather than pulling every style defined in the file including unused library styles, StyleSync walks the document tree and extracts only the styles that are actually applied to elements. This keeps your Framer style panel clean and relevant.
copy.value: Paste any Figma file URL and StyleSync scans the entire document for actively-used styles. Rather than pulling every style defined in the file including unused library styles, StyleSync walks the document tree and extracts only the styles that are actually applied to elements. This keeps your Framer style panel clean and relevant.

copy.original: Framer already lets you design light and dark variants of your Color Styles, but by default a visitor only ever sees the version that matches their device. There is no built-in way to give them a switch — and rolling your own means writing code that rewrites stylesheets, tracking state across pages, and hoping nothing breaks on export.
copy.value: Framer already lets you design light and dark variants of your Color Styles, but by default a visitor only ever sees the version that matches their device. There is no built-in way to give them a switch — and rolling your own means writing code that rewrites stylesheets, tracking state across pages, and hoping nothing breaks on export.

copy.original: Smart Theme Switch handles all of it. Drop the component onto any page, point it at your brand colors, and it becomes a live control that flips your entire site between light and dark on a single tap. It reads the light and dark styles Framer already generates and re-applies the set the visitor chooses — so every background, text color, border, and surface repaints together, with zero manual wiring.

copy.original: Transform your existing website into a refined, high-performing experience. We rebuild from the core, improving visuals, usability, and conversion flow while keeping your brand identity intact.
copy.value: Transform your existing website into a refined, high-performing experience. We rebuild from the core, improving visuals, usability, and conversion flow while keeping your brand identity intact.

copy.original: A redesign is not a repaint. Sites usually underperform for reasons that have nothing to do with how they look: the navigation buries what people came for, the homepage explains the company instead of the offer, the pages load slowly on a phone, or the path from interest to enquiry has three unnecessary steps in it. New visuals on top of those problems produce a better-looking site that converts exactly as badly.
copy.value: A redesign is not a repaint. Sites usually underperform for reasons that have nothing to do with how they look: the navigation buries what people came for, the homepage explains the company instead of the offer, the pages load slowly on a phone, or the path from interest to enquiry has three unnecessary steps in it. New visuals on top of those problems produce a better-looking site that converts exactly as badly.

copy.original: So the work starts with an audit rather than a moodboard. We go through the current structure, the analytics if you have them, and the journeys that actually matter to the business, and identify what is costing you enquiries. That review is shared with you before any design begins, so you can see the reasoning rather than just the result.
copy.value: So the work starts with an audit rather than a moodboard. We go through the current structure, the analytics if you have them, and the journeys that actually matter to the business, and identify what is costing you enquiries. That review is shared with you before any design begins, so you can see the reasoning rather than just the result.

copy.original: Your brand comes through the process intact. Where you have an established identity — a logo, a palette, a typeface, a way of speaking — it is kept and applied more consistently than before. Redesigns that discard recognisable brand assets tend to confuse returning visitors for no gain.
copy.value: Your brand comes through the process intact. Where you have an established identity — a logo, a palette, a typeface, a way of speaking — it is kept and applied more consistently than before. Redesigns that discard recognisable brand assets tend to confuse returning visitors for no gain.

copy.original: The part most redesigns get wrong is the handover. Changing your URLs without mapping the old ones to the new can erase search rankings you spent years earning. Existing addresses are preserved where they can be and redirected where they cannot, page titles and descriptions are carried across, and the structured data is rebuilt so the new site inherits what the old one had rather than starting from zero.
copy.value: The part most redesigns get wrong is the handover. Changing your URLs without mapping the old ones to the new can erase search rankings you spent years earning. Existing addresses are preserved where they can be and redirected where they cannot, page titles and descriptions are carried across, and the structured data is rebuilt so the new site inherits what the old one had rather than starting from zero.

copy.original: Most redesigns run two to six weeks depending on page count and how much of the content is being rewritten. If the existing site is large, we will usually suggest phasing it — the pages that earn the most attention first — rather than holding everything back for one launch.

copy.original: Speed is not a technical preference, it is a commercial one. People abandon slow pages, and they abandon them fastest on the mobile connections most traffic now arrives on. copy.original: The work is measurement-led rather than a checklist. copy.original: The fix is to stop making those decisions page by page. Colour, type, spacing, radius and elevation are defined once as a system, and every page draws from it. copy.value: Photofolio is a photography portfolio website for a portrait, family, event and wedding photographer. The first screen is a contact sheet you can drag, and every page keeps the photographs as the interface.

copy.original: A photographer needed a site where the interface disappears. Photography sites fail in two directions: chrome that competes with the images, or minimalism so severe the work floats without context. The brief: photographs first, with just enough structure that a visitor can still find a service, a price and a way to book.

copy.original: We built a dark, quiet frame around the work. Every project is one real session, so a page never mixes light or people. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis.

copy.original: Smart Theme Switch is a Framer code component that adds a one-tap light and dark mode toggle to your site. It flips every page instantly, remembers each visitor's choice, and works with your existing Framer Color Styles automatically. No custom code, no duplicated styles, no flash of the wrong theme.
copy.value: Smart Theme Switch is a Framer code component that adds a one-tap light and dark mode toggle to your site. It flips every page instantly, remembers each visitor's choice, and works with your existing Framer Color Styles automatically. No custom code, no duplicated styles, no flash of the wrong theme.

copy.original: Framer already lets you design light and dark variants of your Color Styles, but by default a visitor only ever sees the version that matches their device. There is no built-in way to give them a switch — and rolling your own means writing code that rewrites stylesheets, tracking state across pages, and hoping nothing breaks on export.
copy.value: Framer already lets you design light and dark variants of your Color Styles, but by default a visitor only ever sees the version that matches their device. There is no built-in way to give them a switch — and rolling your own means writing code that rewrites stylesheets, tracking state across pages, and hoping nothing breaks on export.

copy.original: Smart Theme Switch handles all of it. Drop the component onto any page, point it at your brand colors, and it becomes a live control that flips your entire site between light and dark on a single tap. It reads the light and dark styles Framer already generates and re-applies the set the visitor chooses — so every background, text color, border, and surface repaints together, with zero manual wiring.
copy.value: Smart Theme Switch handles all of it. Drop the component onto any page, point it at your brand colors, and it becomes a live control that flips your entire site between light and dark on a single tap. copy.original: StyleSync is a Framer plugin that extracts actively-used styles from your Figma files, design token files, and websites, and imports them directly into Framer as native color and text styles. No manual copying, no missed tokens, no mismatched values.
copy.value: StyleSync is a Framer plugin that extracts actively-used styles from your Figma files, design token files, and websites, and imports them directly into Framer as native color and text styles. No manual copying, no missed tokens, no mismatched values.

copy.original: Every design workflow involves moving styles between tools. Designers maintain color palettes and typography in Figma, developers define tokens in CSS or JSON, and production sites carry their own computed styles. Getting those values into Framer accurately and quickly is tedious work done manually.

copy.original: StyleSync automates that transfer. It reads your styles from wherever they live, shows you a preview with full control over what gets imported, and injects only the styles you select directly into your Framer project as native color styles and text styles, accessible from any element in the canvas.

Rather than pulling every style defined in the file including unused library styles, StyleSync walks the document tree and extracts only the styles that are actually applied to elements. This keeps your Framer style panel clean and relevant.

brief.en: A private heathland club wanted a website that works as hard as its starter. Visitors need to see weekday availability and green fees at once, prospective members need honest subscriptions and a joining process, and the course itself had to be shown properly rather than as a gallery of stock fairways.

approach.en: We built the site around the round itself. A full-width hero puts the golfer and the club name together, the homepage carries a working tee sheet, every hole has its own aerial with yardages drawn over it, and membership fees are set out as a simple table. Type is tall and compact, in forest green with one lime accent.

outcome.en: The site now answers the practical questions in the order golfers ask them: a tee time for a guest, the fees, what the course plays like hole by hole, how to join, and where to lunch afterwards. The course, visitors, membership, academy and clubhouse each have a clear page of their own.

about.en:
The site includes Home, the Course with a hole-by-hole guide and scorecard, Visitors with weekday tee-time booking and green fees, Membership with subscriptions and the joining process, the Academy with coaching and lesson prices, the Clubhouse with menus and private dining, and Contact with directions, plus Privacy and Terms pages.

The visual direction is bright and bold: white pages, forest green and a single lime accent, set in Sofia Sans Extra Condensed capitals. The hero sets the club name behind the tree line with the golfer in front of it, every hole has an aerial with its yardages and hazards drawn over it, and square-edged panels replace shadows and rounded pills.

Built as a fast static site in Astro with plain TypeScript, Wrenmoor Heath loads quickly on a phone at the first tee, keeps motion to quiet reveals and respects reduced-motion settings. The tee-time, application and enquiry forms are built in.

brief.en: A timepiece retailer spanning luxury and smart categories needed one store that serves two shopping mindsets — the browser savouring craft and the buyer comparing specs — without splitting into two experiences.

approach.en: We organised the store around honest merchandising: category-first browsing, disciplined filtering, and product pages that give each watch the photographic space of a display case. Members’ accounts and integrated payments make the return visit as smooth as the first.

outcome.en: Both shoppers get their store: the connoisseur can wander, the decider can filter, and each reaches checkout without friction. The catalogue scales cleanly across categories, and the presentation holds its polish from hero to receipt.

about.en:
Watches is a fully functional eCommerce website crafted to deliver a premium and user-friendly online shopping experience. The design focuses on clarity, trust, and ease of navigation, allowing customers to explore a curated collection of timepieces effortlessly.

The homepage introduces the brand with a bold hero banner, highlighting key offers and featured collections. Visitors can shop by category, browse top sellers, or explore special deals through a structured grid layout. Each product card features pricing, availability, and variant details for quick decisions.

The store page integrates advanced filtering by type, price, and material, ensuring users can refine their search smoothly. The product detail page includes images, specifications, quantity selection, and an instant add-to-cart experience, leading directly to a clean and secure checkout flow.

The footer reinforces brand reliability with policy links, contact details, and payment method visuals, creating a complete retail environment that feels both modern and trustworthy.

Developed using Wix Studio’s eCommerce tools, the site combines visual appeal with performance, optimized for mobile responsiveness, easy updates, and high conversion potential.

brief.en: A studio that sells websites needs a website that sells itself. The brief: show the work on the real sites, put the prices in the open, and make the first call easy to book.

approach.en: We built it light and direct: one orange against paper and ink, a portrait hero that follows the cursor, and every section answering one question a buyer asks. Work is shown as the client's own homepage, prices sit in a table, and the process is laid out as twelve weeks. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis.

outcome.en: A site that reads like the studio works: clear, quick to scan and honest about cost. Visitors can compare three fixed prices, open any of twelve case pages, and book a 30-minute call from any screen.

about.en:
The home page opens on a portrait that turns to follow the cursor beneath a giant wordmark, then moves through a one-sentence introduction, the platforms the studio builds on, four launches shown on the real sites, five services, three fixed prices, a twelve-week process, client words and the questions people ask first.

Behind it sit twelve works with their own case pages, five service pages with prices and timelines, six ready-made templates, a blog of studio notes, an about page that tells the studio's story year by year, and a four-step enquiry form.

The type is Inter and Spline Sans Mono, the palette is paper, ink and a single orange, and the site is fully responsive.

brief.en: A growth agency that makes the creative and buys the media wanted a site that proves both at once. Buyers spending £50k to £1.5m a month needed to see real ads, the result each one produced, what the work costs and who does it, without wading through an agency template of logos and adjectives.

approach.en: Show the work as the ad. The hero is a story player with the headline crossing it, case studies open on the ad formats with the result in mono, the studio line resolves from a knockout that reads one room, and a pinned scene cuts forty-two hooks to the three that won. Services run as one plan with a bar sized by price, the fee is a slider that prices a month of spend, and the contact form is a sentence that finishes itself.

outcome.en: A buyer can watch an ad play, read the number it earned, price their own month of spend and ask for a growth audit in a few minutes. The pages stay light and quick on a phone, and every case study, service, role and result is a content file the client edits without touching the design.

about.en:
The site includes Home, Work with six case studies, Services, Agency and Contact, plus Privacy, Terms and 404 pages.

The visual direction is bold and editorial: a paper page, ink and one signal orange, Mona Sans set wide for headlines and Geist Mono for figures, and ads shown in their real 9:16, 4:5 and 1:1 formats. The hero is a story player with the headline crossing it, the studio line resolves from a knockout that reads one room, and a pinned scene cuts forty-two ad hooks down to three winners.

Built as a fast static site in Astro with plain TypeScript, GSAP and Lenis, Upwell keeps its case studies, services, team, roles, results and FAQs as one content file per item, respects reduced-motion settings and works on a phone. The pricing slider and the sentence-style contact form are built in.

brief.en: A neighbourhood groomer needed a website that answers the questions owners are nervous about before booking: what it costs for my dog, how the pet is dried, and who is holding the scissors. Most grooming sites hide prices behind stock photos, so the brief was a cheerful, honest site that shows both.

approach.en: We built Tubwell around price tags, a groom card and house rules. Prices hang on tags by dog size, every pet gets a card with its coat, cut and notes, and a soft pastel palette with hand-lettered touches keeps the tone playful. It runs on WordPress with Elementor, so the team can edit it.

outcome.en: The site now reads like the shop it represents: owners can price a groom, meet the regulars, see how pets are dried and book from the same page. The shop, self-wash tubs and studio each have their place, and everything stays editable so prices and products can change without a designer.

about.en:
The site includes Home, Grooming with the full price list, a booking request page, the Shop with thirteen products, a Studio page with the house rules and directions, and Privacy and Terms pages. Every price tag, groom card and product is its own editable item.

The visual direction uses soft lilac, peach and mint panels with a blue accent, Bricolage headlines and a hand-lettered note face. Pets peek over the service cards, price tags hang on a line and a groom card fans out like a real index card, so the page feels like the counter of a friendly shop.

Built on WordPress with Elementor, Tubwell keeps sections, layouts and content editable, with custom widgets only for the interactive parts such as the price picker, groom cards and bag drawer. Booking requests are saved inside WordPress.

brief.en: A restaurant with genuine character needed a website that tasted like the room: bold, warm, and unmistakably itself. Menus, hours, and reservations had to be effortless to find — but wrapped in an experience that makes the booking feel like it has already begun.

approach.en: We built the site around the photography — saturated dishes against dark, atmospheric grounds — and let cultural typography carry the brand’s voice. Reservations are integrated natively so a table is two taps from the hero, and motion is kept to slow, appetite-adjacent reveals rather than spectacle.

outcome.en: The site now does what a good maître d’ does: sets the mood and removes friction in the same gesture. Diners arrive already sold on the atmosphere, the menu reads as a promise rather than a list, and booking a table takes less time than choosing a starter.

about.en:
Tigre Tigre is a restaurant website designed to capture the authentic character of a modern dining and sake experience. The layout merges elegance with energy — using deep color palettes, textured backgrounds, and full-width imagery that highlight both the cuisine and ambiance of the restaurant.

The hero section immediately immerses visitors in the restaurant’s atmosphere with high-quality visuals and clear branding. The menu structure is presented in a clean, sectioned layout, dividing offerings such as starters, rolls, ramen, cocktails, and desserts for effortless browsing. Each category is paired with vibrant food photography to create an engaging and appetite-driven experience.

The visual hierarchy emphasizes both readability and mood, balancing bold headers with minimalist typography to reflect the sophistication of the venue. The footer section completes the journey with reservation details, contact links, and a social media gallery that enhances user interaction and brand connection.

Developed in Wix Studio, the design prioritizes responsiveness and smooth navigation across devices, ensuring every visitor can explore the restaurant’s offerings seamlessly. The result is a digital dining experience that mirrors the warmth, taste, and cultural depth of Tigre Tigre itself.

brief.en: A creative professional needed a portfolio with a raised voice — high contrast, hard edges, immediate impact — without tipping into noise. Bold is easy; bold and legible is the brief.

approach.en: We committed to contrast as the system: stark grounds, oversized type, and imagery that lands like a poster. The boldness is disciplined by a strict grid and deliberate motion, so every loud element arrives on the beat rather than over it.

outcome.en: The site is remembered — which for a portfolio is the entire job. Work is presented with total confidence, the personality is unmistakable within seconds, and the structure keeps the volume from ever costing clarity.

about.en:
Showin is a dynamic and visually striking portfolio website designed to reflect creativity, confidence, and clarity. Built for freelancers and creative professionals, it combines strong typography, bold contrasts, and structured layouts to present work with precision and impact.

The website includes dedicated sections for Services, Portfolio, Blog, and Contact, each thoughtfully crafted to balance function and style. The homepage introduces the designer’s expertise with a bold hero section and an About Me area that builds trust through personality and experience. The Portfolio and Blog pages are powered by CMS, making it easy to showcase projects, share insights, and manage content effortlessly.

Showin’s design emphasizes usability and visual storytelling. Every element, from project cards and testimonials to blog layouts, reinforces professionalism while keeping the user engaged. With clear navigation, a consistent visual identity, and responsive performance, the site delivers a refined digital experience for clients and collaborators alike.

Built on Wix Studio, Showin serves as both a showcase and a statement, representing the perfect blend of creativity, strategy, and modern design thinking.

summary.en: Summary

brief.en: Edited Brief Give a flight school one site where visitors can compare programs, book a discovery flight and apply to train.

approach.en: Open on the hero, then walk from programs to discovery flights, fleet, pricing and a clear student journey.

outcome.en: A Wix Studio site of eight pages, from the Ascent Pilot Program and pricing to a six-step formal application.

about.en:
RVA Flyers is a complete website for a flight school at Richmond International Airport, a Diamond Flight Center that trains pilots from Private through CFII in Diamond DA40 aircraft with certified flight instructors. It is built around one idea: a first-time visitor should see where pilots begin and find the next step, a tour, a discovery flight or an application, without hunting for it.

The home page opens on a full-screen photo of a Diamond aircraft with the headline Where Pilots Begin and three actions: Book a discovery flight, Apply Now and Request a Tour. Building Pilots With Purpose follows with four figures the school states: 63+ certificates issued this year, 10 modern aircraft, an 89% overall checkride pass rate and 9 certified flight instructors. Flight Training Programs presents the Ascent Pilot Program, an accelerated multi-engine add-on and the Private, Instrument and Commercial courses. Then come a tour invitation, two discovery flights (The Adventurer and The Aviator), a Getting Started enquiry form, the six steps from interested to enrolled, Our Fleet, resources, three student stories, the Diamond Flight Center section and the team of eight instructors.

Behind it sit a Flight Training Programs page, the Ascent Pilot Program page, Pricing with hourly aircraft and instructor rates, a Student Journey page, Resources and FAQ, Contact, and a six-step Formal Application.

The type is Manrope Regular throughout. The palette is black and white with one blue for the main buttons. The site was built for the school's owner, Josh Das, on Wix Studio.

brief.en: A premium restaurant needed its website to match the standard of its service — the digital equivalent of a well-set table. Ambience had to come through the screen, while the menu and reservations stayed one intuitive gesture away.

approach.en: We composed the site like the room: considered lighting in the photography, an elegant typographic menu built on the CMS, and native reservations so the impulse to book never has to survive a context switch. Motion is slow and assured, in the register of hospitality.

outcome.en: Guests now arrive with expectations the room can meet, because the site set them honestly. The menu is a pleasure rather than a PDF, tables get booked in the moment of decision, and the restaurant updates its offering as easily as rewriting the specials board.

about.en:
Restra is a premium restaurant website experience crafted to capture the warmth, sophistication, and atmosphere of fine dining. The goal of the project was to create a digital presence that feels as inviting as the restaurant itself, blending rich imagery, elegant typography, and intuitive user flow to elevate the brand’s identity.

The website features dedicated pages including Home, Menu, Reservation, About, and Restaurant Info, each designed with a guest first approach. Every section uses warm tones, cinematic visuals, and carefully structured content to highlight the restaurant’s dishes, story, and dining environment. From detailed menu layouts to immersive hero sections, the design guides visitors smoothly while keeping the experience visually engaging.

A clear reservation system, polished food displays, and storytelling driven content make the website both functional and emotionally appealing. Thoughtful spacing, subtle shadows, and a refined dark theme come together to create a luxurious look that reflects the restaurant’s character.

Built in Wix Studio, Restra ensures seamless responsiveness, high quality media handling, and effortless content updates. The design balances visual richness with usability, making it ideal for modern restaurants looking to strengthen their digital presence, increase reservations, and create a memorable first impression for guests.

brief.en: A counselling practice needed a website for people arriving on a hard day. Every design decision had to lower the threshold: warm without being saccharine, professional without being clinical, and structured so that finding help never adds to the burden.

approach.en: We chose warmth as the architecture — soft colour, generous space, plain-spoken headings — and made the path to reaching out impossible to lose. Services are explained in the client’s language rather than the profession’s, and the contact flow asks for the minimum a first step requires.

outcome.en: The site now does the first session’s first minute: it makes the visitor feel expected. People in difficulty can understand the offer, feel the tone, and reach out — and the practice presents itself with the same care it promises in the room.

about.en:
Recapture Life Counseling is a complete counseling and speaking services website solution designed to build trust, emotional connection, and clarity for visitors seeking personal growth and support. The project was created with a strong focus on warmth, approachability, and usability, delivering a digital experience that feels personal, safe, and action-oriented.

The website includes essential pages such as Home, About, Services, and Contact, each structured to guide users smoothly through the counselor’s background, approach, and service offerings. Clear content hierarchy and focused service sections help visitors quickly understand available support areas such as depression counseling, anxiety support, relationship guidance, leadership coaching, and speaking engagements.

The visual direction combines earthy tones, soft imagery, and clean layouts to create a calm and reassuring atmosphere. Structured service blocks, personal story sections, and strong call-to-action areas encourage users to explore services and take the next step with confidence.

Built with responsiveness and scalability in mind, the site performs seamlessly across devices and allows easy updates to services and content. The result is a compassionate, professional digital presence that aligns with the mission of modern counseling and coaching brands focused on transformation, clarity, and human connection.

brief.en: A photographer needed a site where the interface disappears. Photography sites fail in two directions: chrome that competes with the images, or minimalism so severe the work floats without context. The brief: photographs first, with just enough structure that a visitor can still find a service, a price and a way to book.

approach.en: We built a dark, quiet frame around the work. The home page opens on a contact sheet you can drag, then moves through a pinned statement, a gallery you move through sideways, four services and a film strip of how a shoot works. Every project is one real session, so a page never mixes light or people. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis.

outcome.en: The site behaves like a well-hung exhibition: the eye moves from image to image with nothing pulling at its sleeve. Services show a clear price and a one-page plan, projects open into a gallery that respects each photograph's shape, and the journal gives the practice a voice between commissions.

about.en:
Photofolio is a complete website for a portrait, family, event and wedding photographer, built with Astro and designed to put the photographs first. A dark, calm layout keeps the colour in the images, and nothing decorative competes with them.

The home page opens on a contact sheet you can drag, then moves through a pinned statement that changes rooms as you scroll, a gallery you move through sideways, four services with prices, a film strip showing how a shoot works, client notes and the journal.

Each of the thirteen projects is a single session, shown in a gallery that respects the shape of every photograph and opens into a lightbox. Services, About, Journal and Contact share one type system: Host Grotesk for headlines and Geist Mono for captions.

The site is fully responsive and built from structured content, so sessions, services and journal notes can be added without touching the layout.

brief.en: A BPO that runs customer support, trust and safety and back office for consumer brands wanted a site that sounds like the people it hires. Buyers needed to see how a team is built, where it sits, what it costs and who answers, without a long sales form in the way.

approach.en: Every reply has a name. The hero pairs a customer message with the agent who answers it, in a serif for the customer and a wide grotesk for the reply, over portraits of the four studios. Services, a follow-the-sun view, the six-week process, a weekly report, published rates and a team estimator follow.

outcome.en: A buyer can see the three kinds of work, the four studios and how the queue is handed over, read a real weekly report, price a team and ask for a plan in a few minutes. The pages stay light and quick for a visitor on any device.

about.en:
The site includes Home, Services with customer support, trust and safety and back office, How we work, Rates, Plan a team, Locations, Clients with three case studies and Careers, plus Privacy, Terms and 404 pages.

The visual direction is calm and editorial: a paper page, ink and one ultramarine accent, a light italic serif for the customer and Mona Sans for the reply, daylight photography of real teams, square panels and no shadows. Headlines resolve line by line, photographs reveal behind a curtain and the studios hand the queue over as the clock turns.

Built as a fast static site in Astro with plain TypeScript, GSAP and Lenis, Parley respects reduced-motion settings and works on a phone. The team estimator, plan-a-team form and careers filters are built in.

brief.en: Make a magazine site read like a printed front page while 13 stories, a podcast and an issue stay easy to find.

approach.en: Set the name as a giant masthead, lead with a story slider, and keep one red accent across white pages.

outcome.en: A complete magazine with sections, articles, contributors, a podcast and a print page, ready to reuse.

about.en:
Oriel is a complete online magazine for stories on how we live now: 13 stories across five sections, a print issue, a podcast and a Sunday newsletter. It is built around one idea: a printed front page on screen, with the name set as one very large masthead, white pages, black type and a single red accent. All stories, people and prices are demo content.

The home page opens on the masthead and a lead-story slider, then an Editor's pick, Night trains are back, and they're full. The latest lists the newest stories with an All 13 stories link, followed by Most read this week, Issue 07 The Slow Issue (212 pages), Oriel Radio with Episode 48, What makes a room feel calm, and The people who write Oriel. Five good stories, every Sunday, the newsletter sign-up, closes the page.

Behind it sit an All stories page, a page for each section (Culture, Design, Food, Technology, Travel), article pages with the writer, date and reading time, a Contributors page with eight profiles, Oriel Radio, a page for the print edition, About, Privacy and Terms.

The type is Gambarino for the masthead, headlines and card titles, and Geist for text. The palette is white, black and grey with Oriel red, and each section has its own label colour. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis.

brief.en: A Felixstowe freight forwarder running containers since 1974 had a site that said little about price or progress. Importers wanted a rate they could trust, sailing cut-offs they could plan around and a way to follow a box without phoning the desk, all from one team and not a queue.

approach.en: The hero is a live sentence: pick a container, a load port and a destination and the rate and next cut-off update in place over aerial terminal photography. Services, a filterable sailings table, a three-step rate request and a container tracker sit behind it in a calm, large-type layout.

outcome.en: A shipper can price a lane, see the next sailings, request a firm rate and track a container from one site, with a named desk and a phone number on every page. The site stays quick on a phone at the yard gate.

about.en:
The site includes Home, Services with a sample invoice for each of five services, Quote with a three-step rate request, Sailings with a filterable cut-off table, Track for container numbers and booking references, Company and Contact, plus Privacy and Terms pages.

The visual direction is plain and confident: a light fog page, ink and one rust-orange accent, Archivo in sentence case with IBM Plex Mono for container numbers, and aerial and quayside photography. The hero is a sentence you edit in place, and tabs, filters and accordions animate both ways.

Built as a fast static site in Astro with plain TypeScript, Norholm Freight keeps motion calm, respects reduced-motion settings and works on a phone at the yard gate. The rate, sailings, tracking and contact forms are built in.

brief.en: A Swiss watchmaker needed a store that sells the way a boutique does — unhurried, precise, certain of its worth. Most ecommerce templates optimise for volume and noise; mechanical timepieces need the opposite: room, restraint, and product photography treated like the product itself.

approach.en: We built a gallery-first storefront in Wix Studio: collections for men’s, women’s, sport, and smart lines, each presented on deep neutral grounds with the watch as the only saturated object on screen. Payments, filtering, and category browsing run on the platform’s commerce layer, so the elegance sits on proven checkout plumbing.

outcome.en: The store reads as a showroom and functions as a machine — browsing feels like being handed the watch, while cart and checkout behave exactly as buyers expect. Collections scale without crowding, and the brand’s restraint survives every screen size.

about.en:
The Meridian website is a full eCommerce build for a fictional Genève watchmaker, designed to feel closer to a boutique showroom than a typical online store. The homepage leads with a cinematic hero and a considered product narrative — "Precision, worn quietly" — before moving into curated collections (Best Sellers, New Arrivals, Sale) and a dedicated craft section that walks through materials, movement, and water resistance.

Rather than presenting a flat product grid, the site layers storytelling throughout: a limited-edition GMT spotlight, a five-point craft breakdown, and a concierge-style service section covering warranty, servicing, and delivery. Category navigation (Luxury, Sports, Smart, Ladies) sits alongside a full catalogue, giving the store both a browsable structure and a strong editorial point of view.

The visual language stays disciplined — deep blues and steel tones, generous whitespace, and typography that reads more editorial than retail — reinforcing the "engineered to outlast trends" positioning. A newsletter capture ("Correspondence") closes the experience, keeping the tone consistent with the rest of the site rather than reading as a bolt-on marketing form.

brief.en: A creative agency needed a site elegant enough to promise taste and organised enough to prove process. Agencies sell judgement; the site had to demonstrate it in every margin, transition, and line of copy.

approach.en: We composed Lumora around refinement: a restrained palette, precise typography, and immersive imagery that carries the emotion while the layout keeps order. Services, work, and contact flow as one continuous argument, with animation as punctuation rather than performance.

outcome.en: The site now makes the agency’s case before the first meeting — visitors experience the standard of finish the team would bring to their brand. Enquiries arrive better qualified, because the site has already communicated what working together looks like.

about.en:
Lumora is a thoughtfully designed agency website built to showcase the balance between creativity and strategy. Every section is crafted to reflect the studio’s refined visual language, from the soft gradients and structured grid to the minimal yet expressive typography.

The homepage establishes the agency’s identity with bold statements and smooth transitions that highlight both expertise and personality. Each internal page maintains design harmony while serving a unique purpose: the Services page details the agency’s creative offerings, the Portfolio presents their best work, and the About page introduces the team and ethos.

The layout focuses on usability and engagement, combining strong visual storytelling with functional clarity. Subtle animations and consistent spacing enhance readability while maintaining a premium aesthetic. Designed in Wix Studio, Lumora stands as a benchmark for professional, high-performing digital agency websites, built to attract, inform, and inspire.

brief.en: Make an agency site that sells the idea loud and the craft quiet: a lit portrait up front, cases that lead with a number, and prices and people shown before the first call.

approach.en: One backlit portrait and a giant headline open a near-black, grid-ruled site, with every case written as brief, idea, execution and result and a figure leading each one.

outcome.en: A complete six-page agency site with a case study template, a journal and a brief form, ready to start a conversation from the first screen.

about.en:
Loudwell is a complete website for an independent marketing agency in London. It is built around one line: loud ideas, quiet craft.

The home page opens on a backlit portrait under that line, then shows three results, six cases, short films made for the feed, one featured launch, four ways in, brief to launch in twelve weeks, a client voice, the brands it made louder, the 38 people on the floor and the latest notes.

Behind it sit a work page with every case in full, a case study template that leads with the result, a services page with a price for each service and a choice of project or retainer, a studio page with the team and a day on the floor, a journal with posts, and a brief form with a map to the studio.

The type is Inter Tight for headlines and text, with Geist Mono for the labels. The palette is near black, off-white and ember, ruled on a hairline grid with plus marks, and the imagery is lit portrait and product photography. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis.

brief.en: A travel brand that sells bespoke planning has nothing to show but photographs everyone else also has. The site had to make an atelier of eleven planners feel deliberate and rare, without listing packages like a tour operator.

approach.en: We built six pages around one idea: every journey is drawn, not sold. A full-screen hero, a register of the routes open now, an atlas of forty-one countries, and a timeline showing how seven months actually overlap.

outcome.en: The site now reads as a studio rather than a catalogue. A visitor can judge the method in a single scroll, see which travel windows are still free, and send an enquiry that already carries the shape of the trip.

about.en:
Six pages carry it: a home that opens on a full-screen frame, an Expeditions register of the routes currently open, an Atlas of forty-one countries with a pin for each, The Atelier for the people and the method, a How it works timeline, and an enquiry page shaped like a travel document.

The site is hand-built in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with its typefaces embedded in the page rather than fetched from a CDN, so it opens as readily on a hotel connection as on a desk.

Interaction is used only where it earns its place: a hero search that composes an enquiry, an atlas that opens a country on hover or keyboard, seven months of planning drawn as overlapping bars, and dispatches from past travellers printed like boarding passes.

brief.en: A creative professional needed a portfolio that gets to the point — skills, services, and proof, structured for the thirty seconds a busy prospect actually spends. Minimal, but never empty.

approach.en: We designed a compact narrative: a decisive opening, services stated in plain terms, selected work as evidence, and a single clear invitation to talk. The minimalist language keeps attention on substance; the blog adds depth for anyone who wants it.

outcome.en: The site now works at prospect speed. In one scroll, a visitor knows what is offered, sees it proven, and knows how to start — and the restraint of the design reads as exactly the professionalism it advertises.

about.en:
Launchfolio is a personal portfolio website built to present creative expertise in a clean, organized, and professional way. The design reflects modern simplicity, using clear typography, subtle color accents, and structured spacing to create an elegant visual flow.

The hero section introduces the professional identity with a balanced layout, combining portrait imagery and a precise introduction. The about section follows with personal background, professional focus, and a short downloadable CV for quick access. The skills section showcases technical proficiency through animated progress visuals, giving a measurable sense of capability.

The services section outlines the professional’s core offerings design, development, writing, and promotion, each displayed with clarity and concise descriptions. The portfolio and blog pages use filter-based navigation, allowing visitors to browse projects and insights by category, while maintaining consistent visual alignment and balance.

The contact section concludes the experience with a simplified form and essential contact details, reinforcing accessibility and professionalism.

Developed in Wix Studio, Launchfolio combines smooth animations, minimal typography, and thoughtful spacing to deliver a strong personal brand identity, perfect for freelancers or designers aiming to showcase their expertise effectively online.

brief.en: A law firm needed gravity without stuffiness. Legal sites usually choose between intimidating tradition and generic corporate polish; Kingswell needed to project authority a client can actually approach — and to work flawlessly for people reading in stressful circumstances.

approach.en: We designed a commanding, quiet interface in Framer: a measured serif-led hierarchy, disciplined colour, and a complete light and dark theme so the site meets readers on their terms. Practice areas are CMS-driven, contact routes are unmissable, and custom code keeps the details exact.

outcome.en: The firm now leads with composure. Practice areas read clearly at a glance, the writing has room to demonstrate expertise, and someone deciding whether to make a difficult phone call meets a site that makes the decision feel safer.

about.en:
Kingswell Law is a complete law firm website solution designed to establish authority, communicate expertise, and convert high-intent visitors into clients through a commanding and premium digital experience. The project was built with a strong focus on editorial design, structured content hierarchy, and a visual language that reflects the credibility and precision expected of a leading legal practice.

The website includes essential pages such as Home, About, Services, Team, Blogs, and Contact, each carefully structured to guide visitors through the firm's capabilities, attorneys, legal insights, and consultation pathways. Clear navigation, well-defined content sections, and direct call-to-action elements help users quickly understand service offerings and take confident next steps.

The visual direction combines a dark editorial aesthetic with cool neutral photography, strong typography, and generous spacing to create a sophisticated and trust-centered experience. Custom AI-generated imagery, consistent color grading across all pages, and carefully crafted copy work together to reinforce the firm's positioning as an experienced, client-first legal practice.

Built with responsiveness and scalability in mind, the platform supports ongoing updates for blog content, team members, and service areas. The result is a refined, future-ready digital presence suited for a premium law firm looking to attract high-value clients and communicate legal authority with clarity and confidence.

brief.en: A custom-home builder needed a site that could carry the weight of its craft. Construction websites tend to fall into two traps: stock-photo sameness or a plain gallery that leaves the work to speak into silence. Ironwood needed its projects framed the way the homes themselves are built — deliberately, with nothing accidental on the page.

approach.en: We built Ironwood in Framer around a warm amber-and-charcoal palette and a confident display face, then let structure do the persuading: full-bleed project photography, a CMS so new builds publish without a designer, and a complete dual theme so the site reads as considered in both light and dark. Custom code covers the details Framer alone would round off.

outcome.en: The finished site presents a builder that clearly sweats the details — because the site visibly does. Projects are browsable by the qualities buyers actually weigh, every page holds the same standard of finish as the hero, and the studio can grow the portfolio from the CMS without touching the design.

about.en:
Ironwood is a complete premium residential construction website solution designed to showcase custom homes, luxury renovations, and exceptional craftsmanship through a refined digital experience. The project was built with a strong focus on editorial design, immersive visual storytelling, and structured user flow, creating a platform that reflects the quality, precision, and attention to detail behind every project.

The website includes dedicated pages such as Home, About, Services, Projects, Individual Project Showcase, Process, and Contact, each carefully organized to guide visitors through the company's expertise, completed work, and client journey. Clear navigation, thoughtfully structured content, and strategically placed calls to action help homeowners explore services and confidently take the next step.

A defining feature of the project is its fully integrated dual-theme experience, where both light and dark modes are individually designed to provide a consistent premium aesthetic rather than relying on simple color inversion. Combined with a CMS-powered project portfolio, responsive layouts, subtle animations, and polished micro-interactions, the website delivers an engaging experience while remaining easy to manage and scale as new projects are completed.

The final result is a sophisticated digital platform that strengthens Ironwood's brand identity, showcases its craftsmanship with confidence, and provides prospective clients with a seamless experience that reflects the same level of quality found in every home the company builds.

brief.en: Executive coaching is sold on trust, and most coach websites offer a headshot, a wall of quotes and a contact form. Ines needed a site that lets a busy CEO see how she works, what it costs and what changes for clients in a few minutes, before they ever pick up the phone.

approach.en: We led with a full-bleed portrait and a one-line promise, then answered doubts in the order a CEO has them: familiar problems, four programmes with fixed monthly fees and a twelve-month method in four phases. A cream page with navy panels and saffron accents keeps it warm and serious.

outcome.en: The site now does the first meeting’s work: a founder can recognise their problem, see the fees and the shape of a year, read results from client case studies and request a discovery call in minutes. It runs on WordPress with Elementor, so Ines can edit every section herself.

about.en:
The site includes Home, Coaching with four programmes, Approach, Results with four client case studies, About, a Journal of short articles, Contact, Privacy and Terms pages, with a discovery call form on every path.

The visual direction pairs a cream page with deep navy panels and saffron accents, Host Grotesk headlines with an italic serif for emphasis and a large portrait-led hero. A pinned twelve-month timeline, a results slider and a working-week chart give the page movement without noise.

Built on WordPress with Elementor, almost everything is a native, editable section, with custom elements only for the forms and a few drawn objects, so Ines can change copy, fees and pages herself.

brief.en: A healthcare provider needed a site patients could trust at first glance and navigate at second. Health information punishes clutter: the design had to be clean enough to reassure, structured enough to answer, and careful never to feel clinical to the point of coldness.

approach.en: We designed around clarity of next step — services legible from the landing view, clear pathways to contact, and a tone that stays warm inside a disciplined layout. A CMS keeps service content maintainable, and custom code handles the interactions the platform alone would approximate.

outcome.en: The site now reads the way patients hope the practice operates: organised, considered, and human. Services are findable without hunting, enquiries have an obvious path, and the practice can keep information current without a rebuild.

about.en:
HealthCore is a complete healthcare website solution built to establish trust, clarity, and connection between patients and medical professionals. The design focuses on simplicity, professionalism, and ease of use, ensuring visitors can find essential healthcare information quickly and confidently.

The website includes key sections such as Home, About, Services, Doctors, and Contact — each crafted with a patient-first approach. Clear typography, accessible layouts, and calm color tones create a sense of care and reliability. The interface integrates structured content blocks that highlight key medical services, doctor profiles, and telemedicine options, making it easy for users to explore and engage.

With thoughtful responsiveness and dynamic CMS integration, HealthCore allows effortless content updates for departments, specialists, and testimonials. Its design blends visual consistency with functional depth, offering a digital foundation suited for modern medical practices, clinics, and health professionals aiming to enhance their online presence and patient experience.

brief.en: A family-run roofing company needed a website that earns trust before the first site visit. Homeowners rarely know what a roof should cost or what the work involves, so the site had to explain the process plainly, show real finished roofs and make booking an inspection easy.

approach.en: We built the site around the paperwork homeowners actually receive: an inspection report, a written scope, a daily build log and a warranty. An asphalt and felt-paper palette with a hi-vis accent, Manrope type, a materials library and a cost estimator keep every page practical.

outcome.en: The site now works like a well-run job: services, materials and projects are explained in plain terms, costs can be estimated before a call, and booking an inspection takes a minute. The pages share one system, so new projects and articles slot in cleanly.

about.en:
The site includes Home, six service pages covering replacement, repairs, storm damage, inspections, gutters and ventilation, a materials library with a comparison table, a projects index with detailed case studies, About, a storm damage guide, a full cost estimator, a roofing journal and a contact page with inspection booking.

The visual direction pairs an asphalt ink and felt-paper palette with a hi-vis lime accent taken from the crew’s shirts, set in Manrope with generous spacing. A giant wordmark hero, job-sheet details on project cards and hairline lists keep the site practical and calm rather than salesy.

Built as a fast static site with smooth scrolling, roof-pitch image transitions and reduced-motion support, Halden stays quick and accessible on every device, and its shared page system makes new services, projects and articles easy to add.

brief.en: Give one hundred pieces a single calm look, in nine colours on one plain studio backdrop with one oxblood accent.

approach.en: Put every piece on one studio backdrop, keep oxblood as the one accent, and show each piece in its colours.

outcome.en: A complete clothing store with filters, product pages, accounts and a bag, also rebuilt as a Shopify theme.

about.en:
Halcy is a complete online store for good clothes in calm colours: one hundred pieces for women and men, in nine colours dyed to one recipe and knitted at six family mills near Porto. It is built around one idea: a quiet, light, photo-led page where exactly one flash of oxblood appears, so the colour you notice is the one the shop chooses.

The home page opens on the headline Good clothes, calm colours, with a shop-the-look block of five pieces at $550. A short statement on the nine colours follows, then New this autumn with Women and Men tabs, Shop by category (Knitwear, Shirts, Trousers, Outerwear), and Calm colours, one flash of oxblood. Knitted to shape, linked by hand shows the Merino-Cotton Crew with colour options and a size selector. Most worn, Worn for years, not seasons with customer notes, Six family mills, an hour from Porto, A week of good clothes ($575 for six pieces, Monday to Weekend) and a Letters from the mills sign-up finish the page.

Behind it sit the shop and its collection pages, 100 pieces split into Women 45, Men 40 and Accessories 15 with filters, sort and colour shortcuts, product pages with a gallery per colour, a size guide and reviews, Our mills, About, Help, Search, a customer account and a bag.

The type is Archivo, one family, where the width contrast between narrow text and wide headlines is the signature. The palette is chalk, stone and ink with oxblood as the single accent. Built with Astro and Lenis, and also rebuilt as a Shopify theme.

brief.en: A veterinary clinic needed a website that treats worried owners as gently as it treats their animals. The design had to inspire trust immediately, keep essential actions — services, contact, visits — within easy reach, and stay warm without losing medical credibility.

approach.en: We built the reassurance into the surface: soft tones, approachable typography, and a structure that answers an anxious visitor’s questions in the order they arrive. Contact and enquiry routes are prominent on every page, and gentle motion keeps the experience calm rather than clinical.

outcome.en: The clinic now makes its first good impression before the waiting room. Owners find what they need without hunting, the tone lowers the temperature of a stressful moment, and the practice presents the compassion that is its actual product.

about.en:
Guardian Vets is a thoughtfully designed website for a veterinary clinic, built to convey warmth, care, and professionalism. The design approach centers on emotional connection, combining friendly visuals, rounded layouts, and comforting tones to create a welcoming online presence for pet owners.

The homepage introduces the brand’s compassionate message, “Your Kind of Care,” using large typography and imagery that evoke trust and comfort. The Who We Are section builds credibility by emphasizing the clinic’s long-standing experience and commitment to quality veterinary services. The Our Values and Services sections highlight the clinic’s philosophy and offerings, including vet care, grooming, urgent care, and boarding, through clean iconography and structured layouts.

A well-placed call-to-action area allows users to book appointments or reach out easily, supported by a contact form that simplifies client communication. The footer ties the design together with brand colors, essential links, and social media integration, maintaining a polished and cohesive look.

Developed in Wix Studio, the Guardian Vets website balances accessibility and warmth with professional presentation. It not only strengthens the clinic’s digital identity but also delivers a seamless, trust-driven user experience for both new and returning pet owners.

brief.en: A sustainability initiative needed to turn concern into action — which means a content site that informs without lecturing and inspires without vagueness. The design had to make heavy subject matter feel light enough to keep reading.

approach.en: We built an editorial structure with clean visuals and a natural palette, organising the content so a reader always has a next step — learn, act, or share. The blog is the engine; the design keeps it calm, credible, and quick to scan.

outcome.en: The site now presents environmental content people actually finish reading. Information is structured for momentum rather than guilt, and the initiative has a platform that grows its message post by post.

about.en:
GreenEarth is a modern, purpose-driven website created to inspire and inform audiences about sustainability and environmental responsibility. The design combines a soft, nature-inspired palette with balanced typography and organic shapes to create a sense of calm, trust, and connection to nature.

Each page is built to educate and engage. The Home page introduces the organization’s mission to foster eco-friendly innovation, while the Projects section showcases ongoing campaigns that address air, water, and soil restoration. The Insights and Blog pages provide informative articles on renewable energy, carbon neutrality, and sustainable development — supported by a clear filtering and search system for better user experience.

The Get Involved page is structured to encourage participation through volunteering, donations, and information sharing, reinforcing GreenEarth’s community-driven approach. A subscription-based newsletter in the footer extends the website’s impact by keeping visitors informed about new initiatives and updates.

Designed in Wix Studio, GreenEarth balances visual storytelling with accessibility and structure. It stands as a digital platform for advocacy and action, embodying environmental consciousness through thoughtful design and functionality.

brief.en: A finance company needed the two qualities that rarely coexist on finance websites: clarity and warmth. The site had to explain confidently, look impeccably ordered, and avoid the interchangeable corporate gloss that makes trust harder rather than easier.

approach.en: We built trust typographically — structured layouts, disciplined hierarchy, generous whitespace — and used a clean, modern palette to keep the tone human. Content is organised around the client’s questions, with the blog handling depth so the pages can stay decisive.

outcome.en: The company now communicates like it manages money: precisely and without drama. Visitors find answers in the order they think of them, and the site’s composure does quiet work on every page toward the only metric that matters in finance — confidence.

about.en:
Future Flow is a professionally crafted finance website designed to communicate trust, clarity, and confidence through a structured and refined digital experience. Every section is intentionally designed to balance credibility with accessibility, using clean layouts, disciplined spacing, and a restrained visual language to support informed decision-making.

The homepage introduces the brand with clear messaging and a confident hierarchy, establishing a sense of reliability from the first interaction. Smooth transitions and purposeful content flow guide users through the brand’s value proposition, while maintaining a calm and reassuring tone. Each internal page serves a distinct role within the ecosystem: the Services page outlines the recovery process with transparency, the About page builds trust through narrative and intent, and the Contact page prioritizes clarity and ease of engagement.

The overall layout emphasizes usability and clarity, combining structured content blocks with subtle motion to enhance engagement without distraction. Typography, spacing, and visual consistency work together to maintain a professional and premium aesthetic throughout. Designed in Wix Studio, Future Flow demonstrates how thoughtful design and strategic structure can elevate a finance-focused website into a clear, trustworthy, and high-performing digital presence.

brief.en: A SaaS marketing site is judged on completeness, not just its hero — a buyer wants to see pricing, integrations, and security posture before they trust a product with their team's data, and most landing-page demos stop at the homepage.

approach.en: Forma was built as twelve full pages rather than one, sharing a single dashboard mockup as the visual through-line. Dark and light themes were designed natively side by side, never one simply inverted from the other.

outcome.en: The result reads as a shipped product rather than a mockup: a visitor moves from the headline through features and pricing into a real sign-up flow, landing on a dashboard preview that matches what was promised.

about.en:
Twelve pages carry the story end to end: a marketing home, Features, Solutions by team, a public Integrations directory, three-tier Pricing, a Changelog that reads like a real one, and Security and legal pages that make the product feel shipped.

The interface runs natively in both a dark and a light theme rather than one inverted from the other, with a purple gradient and the same card language carried consistently from the hero through the pricing table to the dashboard mockups.

An animated product dashboard — task counts, a focus-time chart, a due-today list — stands in for the real app throughout the site, so a visitor evaluates something concrete rather than a single static screenshot on the homepage.

brief.en: A digital designer needed a portfolio that says one clear thing: this person makes considered work. The brief called for minimal layouts and a strong personal narrative — a site that reads as a designer’s point of view, not a template with projects in it.

approach.en: We stripped the site to its essentials and then refined each one: clean grids, deliberate type, and a narrative arc from who to what to proof. The blog extends the point of view in writing, and animation is limited to what helps the eye travel.

outcome.en: The portfolio now carries a signature. Work is framed by a perspective rather than floating free of one, and prospective clients meet a designer whose site demonstrates exactly the judgement they would be hiring.

about.en:
EverCraft is a sleek, personality-driven portfolio website designed to present creative work with clarity and confidence. Built with a refined balance of modern design and usability, the site focuses on delivering a seamless experience across every section — from introduction to contact.

The homepage opens with a bold hero layout that establishes the designer’s identity through impactful typography and well-lit portrait imagery. The services section outlines expertise across UI/UX design, front-end development, and mobile app design, while the experience segment highlights years of practice and completed projects, reinforcing professional credibility.

The portfolio section features a categorized gallery of works, allowing users to explore various creative disciplines through an intuitive, grid-based interface. Complementing this is a blog area dedicated to design insights and project stories, enhancing both engagement and authenticity.

The design language combines warm neutrals, clean grids, and subtle orange accents to create a sense of sophistication and energy. Developed in Wix Studio, EverCraft reflects precision, creativity, and function — a digital space built to showcase skill, personality, and professional excellence.

brief.en: A rugby academy needed a digital front door with the energy of a match day and the structure of a training programme. Parents need clarity — programmes, coaches, enrolment; players need to feel the intensity that makes them want in.

approach.en: We built the energy into the visuals — action photography, strong angles, a confident athletic palette — and the trust into the structure: programmes laid out plainly, pathways to joining made obvious, and a blog for fixtures, results, and academy news.

outcome.en: The academy now recruits on both channels at once: players arrive fired up, parents arrive informed. Enrolment interest lands through a clear route, and the site keeps pace with the season instead of falling behind it.

about.en:
Empire Rugby Academy is a complete sports academy website solution built to promote programs, manage registrations, and showcase coaching, events, and player development across branches. The project was designed with a strong focus on clarity, structure, and action-driven user flow, creating a digital platform that supports both athletes and parents.

The website includes essential sections such as Home, Programs, Coaches, News and Events, and Registration, each organized to guide visitors from discovery to enrollment. Clear content hierarchy and direct call-to-action elements help users quickly understand training options, schedules, and branch details without confusion.

The visual direction uses dynamic sports imagery, bold typography, and strong accent colors to reflect energy and competitiveness. Structured content blocks highlight programs, sponsors, partners, testimonials, and achievements while keeping the layout consistent and easy to navigate.

Built with responsiveness and scalability in mind, the site supports ongoing updates for new programs, camps, announcements, and results. The result is a strong, future-ready digital presence for a performance-focused rugby academy.

brief.en: A Chicago business law firm with 41 lawyers needed a website that earns a general counsel’s trust before the first call: who leads a matter, how it is billed, what past results look like, and a conflict check that does not feel like a form wall. It had to read as established and current, not as another dark, shouting law site.

approach.en: We built the site around one idea, that every word is evidence. A bronze statue and a slow court-seal ring open a cream page set in Gambetta and General Sans, with working tools for booking a strategy call and finding a fixed fee, then a results ledger, partner portraits and a conflict-check letter.

outcome.en: A prospective client can see the six practices and their fee models, meet the partner who would lead the work, read results without client names, and start a conflict check in a few minutes. Seven pages and three articles stay quick on a phone.

about.en:
The site includes Home, Practices with fee models and results, People with seven partners and a directory of all 41 lawyers, Matters with a filterable results ledger, the Firm, Insights with three articles and Contact with a live map, plus Privacy and Disclaimer pages.

The visual direction is warm and professional: a cream page, ink and one bronze accent, Gambetta for headings and General Sans for text, bright daylight photography, square hairline panels instead of shadows and a bronze statue with a rotating court-seal ring in the hero. Every accordion, filter and menu animates both ways.

Built as a fast static site in Astro with plain TypeScript, Ellery Kowal loads quickly on a phone, keeps motion calm and respects reduced-motion settings. The conflict-check, strategy-call and fee-finder tools, and the OpenFreeMap-based contact map, are built in.

brief.en: A multi-disciplinary creative — web design, graphic design, video, 3D — needed one portfolio that didn’t read as four stapled together. The risk with range is incoherence: the site had to prove versatility while feeling like the work of a single, decided sensibility.

approach.en: We gave every discipline the same architectural treatment: one grid, one typographic system, one rhythm of reveal — so a 3D render and a brand identity sit side by side as equals. A CMS keeps all four streams publishable, and custom-coded interactions add the layer of craft the work itself promises.

outcome.en: The portfolio now argues for hiring the person, not just a skill. Visitors can enter through any discipline and leave understanding the whole practice, and the site grows with each new project without diluting its point of view.

about.en:
The Devansh Prakash portfolio website is a multi-disciplinary showcase built to highlight creativity and versatility across various design domains. Designed and developed from scratch, it embodies a dark, cinematic aesthetic that enhances visual storytelling while maintaining professional clarity.

The site introduces a strong personal brand identity, establishing an immediate sense of expertise and modern craftsmanship. Each section is thoughtfully categorized — from website design and 3D modeling to video production and graphic design — allowing visitors to explore a wide range of projects with seamless navigation and fluid transitions.

Dynamic project grids and subtle motion effects keep the browsing experience intuitive and visually appealing. The layout balances minimal design with impactful typography, ensuring every project stands out while maintaining a cohesive visual rhythm.

Beyond aesthetics, the portfolio serves as a functional demonstration of Devansh’s technical and creative range — from interactive web layouts to product renderings and motion visuals. The site acts not only as a digital portfolio but as an evolving representation of creative progression, strategy, and precision-driven design.

brief.en: Show a palace hotel the way a guest meets it, with real atmosphere, while keeping the rooms, the tables, the hammam and the booking easy to find.

approach.en: Cinematic photography leads every page, set under a quiet Bodoni and script type system, and every section ends on one clear step toward a stay.

outcome.en: A complete eight-page hotel site, including a reservation flow with a price breakdown, a confirmation and a calendar file, ready to book from the first screen.

about.en:
The home page moves from the lagoon through the rooms and villas, the abras that cross the water, three tables, the hammam, the grounds, four excursions and a short story of the house, and ends on an availability bar and the reservation.

Six inner pages go further: rooms and villas, dining, the hammam, the palace itself, the excursions beyond the gates and a plan-your-stay page with the details of getting there.

A four-step reservation flow handles the dates, the room, the guest details and a review, then ends on a confirmation with a calendar file, all on the site. It is built with Astro, with GSAP and Lenis for motion and scroll.

brief.en: A yoga studio needed its website to lower a visitor’s heart rate, not raise it — while still doing the unglamorous work of a business: schedules, memberships, bookings, and payments. Calm and capable rarely arrive in the same build.

approach.en: We built the calm into the structure: soft tonal grounds, unhurried motion, and a hierarchy that always answers the next question before it is asked. Underneath, Wix Studio carries the operational load — class booking, a members’ area, payment integration, and a blog for the practice’s voice.

outcome.en: New students can go from first visit to booked class in one sitting, and returning members manage everything without leaving the calm the brand promises. The studio runs its schedule and content itself, and the site stays serene while doing real work.

about.en:
Avara is a complete yoga studio website solution crafted to support mindful living, physical well-being, and modern practice habits. The project was designed with a strong focus on simplicity, calmness, and usability, creating a digital space that feels as grounded and intentional as the studio itself.

The website includes essential pages such as Home, About, Classes, Instructors, Blog, and Contact, each designed to guide visitors naturally through the studio’s offerings. Clear content hierarchy and intuitive navigation ensure users can quickly understand class types, instructor backgrounds, and membership options without friction.

The visual direction blends soft, natural imagery with neutral tones and minimal layouts to evoke calm and balance. Structured sections highlight key class categories, instructor profiles, testimonials, and journal content, allowing visitors to engage at their own pace.

Built with responsiveness and scalability in mind, Avara supports seamless viewing across devices and allows easy content updates for classes, blog posts, and studio information. The result is a refined yet approachable digital presence that aligns with the values of modern yoga studios seeking to connect with their community through clarity, intention, and thoughtful design.

brief.en: Make solar, batteries and EV charging easy to choose, price and book for homes across the South West.

approach.en: Pair a shop with a roof estimator, a live day simulator and a calendar to book a survey, all in a calm night-sky theme.

outcome.en: A static site of five main pages that shows the products, the installs and the guarantees, with light and dark themes.

about.en:
auro is a complete website for a home energy installer founded in Bristol in 2014, fitting solar panels, wind, home batteries and EV chargers across the South West and South Wales. It is built around one idea: solar, storage and charging, designed as one, with one survey, one employed team and one warranty. The company, its people, prices and installs are demo content.

The home page opens on a drawn auro wordmark and a rotating product wheel with a Book a home survey action. Solar, storage and charging, designed as one follows with its headline figures, then Essentials, a shop of panels, batteries, chargers and inverters with a basket drawer. What could your roof do? is a roof estimator with heating, residents, car, battery, yearly use and a roof compass. Built for the weather you actually get leads into From survey to switch-on in about three weeks, in four steps: Survey, Design, Install and Switch on. Your home, live is a day simulator set in Bristol on 14 April, Recent installs, at every scale shows Hollow Combe Vineyard, Quarry Fields and Carn Point Hotel, and the page ends with the questions heard at every survey and a calendar to book a home energy assessment.
