Behind it sit a Shop for solar and wind, batteries and inverters, EV chargers and heat and hot water, with a product page and specification for each, How it works with its guarantees, Installs, and About with the team of 46 employed staff, the 1,900+ systems fitted and the areas covered. Every page has a light and dark theme.

The type is General Sans for headings, Inter for text and Departure Mono for labels and buttons. The site is dark by default with a night-sky gradient, a light theme and one blue accent. It is a static site built in HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

brief.en: Make 73 skincare formulas easy to choose between, with a number on every bottle and every dose printed.

approach.en: Number every formula, print the dose, and add a four-question routine finder plus morning and evening sets.

outcome.en: A complete skincare store with filters, routines, ingredients and a journal, also built as a Shopify theme.

about.en:
Aune is a complete online store for Atlantic skincare from Cascais: 73 formulas numbered in the order they left the lab, with every dose printed on the bottle. It is built around one idea, skin after the sea, so you choose by number and routine and not by claims, and the page reads as calmly as the bottles look.

The home page opens on the headline Skin, after the sea, with links to the range and the routine finder. Pick your number offers three starters: Sea Fennel Serum, Samphire Cream and Mineral Day Fluid SPF 30. Healthy skin, in every detail features the Samphire Cream and the Retinal Night Serum. Three steps, five minutes switches between a morning and an evening routine, each with a set price ($114 and $142). The Reserve presents ten high-dose formulas in heavy glass, from $64. Made slowly, on the Atlantic coast tells the story in three parts: The dose, printed, Grown on this coast and Glass you keep. Not sure where to start? opens the four-question routine finder, and Notes from the coast is a monthly newsletter.

Behind it sit the full shop with filters by category (Cleanse, Tone and essence, Serums, Moisturisers, Face oils, Masks and exfoliants, Eye, Lip, SPF, Body, Sets) and by line (Aune, Reserve and Harbour for men), product pages, the routine finder, an Ingredients index, a Journal, Our story, Help and FAQ, a customer account and a bag.

The type is Noto Serif Display for headlines, with italics carrying the voice, and General Sans for text. The palette is foam, sand, deep green ink and sea green. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis, and also built as a Shopify theme.

brief.en: A digital agency needed a complete web presence that could flex as it grows — services, work, insights, and contact in one coherent system, built so tomorrow’s offering doesn’t require next year’s redesign.

approach.en: We designed a modular system in Wix Studio: consistent section patterns, CMS-driven work and writing, and a visual language tight enough to keep future pages on-brand by default. Animation stitches the sections into one continuous read.

outcome.en: The agency now has a site that scales like a product: new services, projects, and posts slot into place without design debt. Visitors get a clear picture of capability and process, and the team publishes with confidence instead of caution.

about.en:
Agency is a professional digital agency website designed to communicate creativity, capability, and trust. The design emphasizes structure, contrast, and clarity, blending minimal typography with immersive visuals to present the agency’s services and portfolio effectively.

The homepage introduces the agency’s vision with a bold tagline and a showcase of featured projects, supported by animated statistics and partner logos that establish credibility. The About page focuses on the agency’s approach, values, and team culture, complemented by testimonial highlights that build authenticity.

The Services page breaks down offerings like illustration, animation, branding, and web development into clearly defined sections, each supported by strong visuals, value points, and CTA buttons leading to relevant projects. The Work page showcases completed projects dynamically with category filters, helping visitors explore creative outcomes with ease.

The Career page enables easy candidate submissions through structured form fields for portfolios, skills, and resumes, while the Contact page features a sleek inquiry form, a FAQ accordion for quick answers, and a clean call to action to start new collaborations.

Developed in Wix Studio, the website balances smooth animations, responsive layouts, and professional color accents to deliver a premium agency presence that feels both approachable and strategic. Every page reinforces the brand’s mission to help businesses grow through thoughtful design and digital innovation.

brief.en: A design studio needed a portfolio site that could pass its own test — a place whose restraint proves the taste it advertises. The brief was minimalism with consequences: every element had to earn its position, because in a studio’s own site, decoration reads as doubt.

approach.en: We reduced the interface to typography, spacing, and work: a strict grid, a quiet palette, and animation used only to establish sequence. The portfolio runs on a CMS with custom code smoothing the seams, so the studio can publish without breaking the discipline of the layout.

outcome.en: The site functions as the studio’s strongest credential — prospective clients experience the standard before reading a word about it. Projects breathe, the writing has a home, and nothing on the page competes with the work.

about.en:
Aesthica is a complete portfolio website solution designed for creative studios and individuals to present their work with clarity, precision, and a refined visual language. The project was built with a strong focus on minimal design, typography-led layouts, and structured content flow, creating a digital space where the work remains the primary focus.

The website includes essential sections such as Home, Work, Profile, Journal, and Contact, each carefully structured to guide visitors through projects, studio philosophy, and ongoing ideas. Clear navigation and a well-defined content hierarchy allow users to explore work, understand the approach, and connect without distraction.

The visual direction emphasizes clean layouts, strong typography, and generous spacing to create a calm and editorial-style experience. Image-first compositions, structured grids, and minimal interface elements ensure consistency while allowing each project to stand out on its own.

Built with responsiveness and flexibility in mind, Aesthica delivers a seamless experience across devices and allows easy customization of projects, content, and sections. The result is a modern, scalable template suited for creatives who want a timeless and design-focused digital presence.

summary.en: Aveline is a complete dental clinic website solution built to give patients clarity before they ever walk in. The project was designed with a strong focus on tr

brief.en: A dental studio needed a website that removes the two things patients dread before a visit: not knowing what it will cost and not knowing what will happen. Clinic sites usually lean on stock imagery and a phone number, so the brief was a calm site that states its prices and lets patients book without calling.

approach.en: We built Aveline around transparency and pace: every treatment page states its duration, starting price and lead clinician. The look is quiet and clinical-warm, using Geist type, a petrol teal accent and generous whitespace. It runs as a WordPress theme with Elementor widgets, so all content stays editable.

outcome.en: The site now works as one continuous visit: each treatment is explained on its own page, the team is introduced by specialty, and booking runs from treatment to clinician to time slot. The journal gives the practice a voice between appointments, and everything stays editable in WordPress.

about.en:
The website includes essential sections such as Home, Treatments, Specialists, About, Journal, and Booking, each structured to guide visitors through what a treatment involves, who will carry it out, and what it costs. Treatment detail pages, a team directory, and a journal of short practical articles keep the content clear and easy to browse.

The visual direction uses a petrol teal accent on soft off-white grounds, Geist typography, and generous spacing to create a quiet, clinical-warm experience. Photo-led layouts, a hero that fits a laptop screen, and dropdown menus with treatment previews keep navigation light without hiding anything.

Built as a custom WordPress theme with editable Elementor widgets, Aveline lets the practice update treatments, specialists, journal articles, and bookings without touching the design, while a live slot picker and written estimate flow keep the patient journey simple across every device.

summary.en: Stillroom is a complete website for a therapy practice in a Georgian townhouse in Stockbridge, Edinburgh, with eight therapists who see adults and couples in pe

brief.en: People looking for therapy are often overwhelmed before they begin. The brief: make the practice feel calm and human, show who the therapists are and what a session costs, and make the first step a short, free call.

approach.en: We built it bright and quiet: paper, moss and sky with one sorrel accent, one family of type with an italic reserved for a few words, and a photographic set shot in open air and sunlit rooms. Motion follows a slow breath, and every section answers one question a new client asks. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis.

outcome.en: A site that feels like the practice: unhurried, clear and honest about cost. Visitors can see each kind of therapy, meet the eight practitioners, look around the house, compare session fees and book a free fifteen-minute call from any page.

about.en:
Stillroom is a complete website for a therapy practice in a Georgian townhouse in Stockbridge, Edinburgh, with eight therapists who see adults and couples in person and online across the UK. It is built around one idea: a room to breathe.

The home page opens on a woman breathing in the open air beneath a giant serif word, then explains in one sentence what the practice does, shows five ways to start, and walks through how it begins: a free fifteen-minute call, a first session, then your own pace.

Behind it sit a page for each kind of therapy, the practitioners with their own profiles, the house and its rooms, a plain price list from £75 a session, and a booking page for the free call.

The type is Switzer for headings and text, with Instrument Serif italic kept for a few words where the voice softens. The palette is paper, moss, sky and sorrel, and the motion is paced by a breath: four seconds in, six seconds out. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis.

summary.en: Alvara House is a boutique estate agency on the Pacific Northwest coast representing architect-designed homes, and the site was built to sell the way the agency

brief.en: Estate agency websites are organised around filters, floor area and price, which is exactly the language Alvara sells against. Their proposition is authorship: the architect is the product. The site had to read like an architecture publication while still working as a property portal, and had to hold that character across sixteen pages and two themes.

approach.en: Hand-built rather than assembled from a template, so the typography could carry the editorial weight the positioning needs. Listings lead with the architect and the year the house was completed, with bedroom counts demoted to a supporting line. Photography sits at full width and is never cropped to a uniform card. Light and dark were designed as two finished treatments rather than one inverted into the other.

outcome.en: A property site that reads as a publication and still performs as a portal. The collection, neighbourhood and journal sections give the agency somewhere to argue a position rather than only list stock, and the architect credit runs consistently from the index through to each individual house.

about.en:
Alvara House is a boutique estate agency on the Pacific Northwest coast representing architect-designed homes, and the site was built to sell the way the agency actually talks. Every listing credits the architect who drew the house and the year it was completed, treating each property as authored work rather than a set of measurements. The design leans editorial throughout — generous type, full-width photography and a restrained palette — so the site reads closer to an architecture publication than a property portal.

The build runs to sixteen pages: a home page, the full property collection, individual house listings, four service pages, nine neighbourhood guides, partner profiles, a journal with its own article template, careers, an FAQ and the enquiry flow. Each one shares a single type system and grid, so the character holds from the collection index through to a single listing without the layout resetting between sections.

A defining feature is the fully realised dual-theme experience. Light and dark are designed as two finished treatments rather than one inverted into the other, with photography, surface tones and contrast tuned separately in each. Alongside that sit considered scroll and hover motion, a listing architecture that puts authorship above bedroom counts, and an enquiry flow built for a market where buyers ask for drawings rather than brochures.

The result is a property site that reads as a publication and still performs as a portal. The collection, neighbourhood and journal sections give the agency somewhere to argue a position rather than simply list stock, and the architect credit carries consistently from the index through to every individual house.

summary.en: Horizone is a car-rental booking site: a full-screen search hero, a filterable 26-car fleet, live-priced car pages, checkout and an account area.

brief.en: Car-rental sites bury the real price under fees and filters. Horizone needed to feel calm and trustworthy, and to let a visitor search, compare and reserve a car without ever losing track of the total.

approach.en: We built the whole journey, not a landing page: a full-screen search hero, a filterable fleet, a car page with a live price panel, then checkout and confirmation, all in one consistent system of light and type.

outcome.en: The site now behaves like a product. Visitors reach a price they trust in a few taps, the fleet looks consistent car to car, and each of the thirteen pages feels like part of one booking experience.

about.en:
Horizone is a car-rental concept built as a complete booking product rather than a single landing page. A visitor searches a city and dates, compares a fleet of 26 cars, reserves one and lands on a confirmation, all on one site.

The site runs to thirteen pages: a home page with a full-screen hero and booking bar, a filterable fleet, a car page with a gallery and live price panel, checkout, confirmation, an account area, locations across 14 cities, deals, help, an about page and legal. Each one is designed to feel like part of the same journey.

Every car is shown in the same soft studio light so the fleet reads as one collection. A strict radius ladder keeps cards, panels and buttons consistent, and prices show fees and protection up front, so the total never changes at the last step.

Motion stays quiet and purposeful: gentle entrances, a sliding pill in the navigation and swipe rows on phones. The whole site is hand-built, fast, accessible and clear at every screen size.

summary.en: Averleigh is a complete website for a private members’ club in the High Weald of East Sussex, founded in 1897. It makes a first visit, a visiting-golf request a

brief.en: A private members’ club in the High Weald needed a website that suits a membership of 340: the course shown properly, visiting golf by arrangement, and joining by introduction rather than by application form. It had to feel current and calm, never like an old club brochure.

approach.en: We set General Sans large and tight on a light stone page, with cinematic photography and hairline detail. An estate-plan hole viewer opens each of the eighteen holes, visiting and membership run as short enquiries, and the House, the Golf Studio and contact each get a page of their own.

outcome.en: Members, visitors and proposers each find their route within a screen: the course and its eighteen holes, the days and rates for visiting golf, how an introduction works, and where to lunch. Every enquiry goes to the Secretary’s office, and the site stays quiet and fast on a phone.

about.en:
The site includes Home, the Course with an estate-plan viewer for all eighteen holes, Visiting with days and rates, Membership by introduction, the House with its menus, the Golf Studio with its professionals, and Contact, plus Privacy and Terms pages.

The visual direction is modern and restrained: a light stone page, General Sans set large and tight, cinematic photography, hairline rules and square-edged buttons instead of shadows and pills. Headlines resolve word by word out of a blur, and every panel and menu animates both ways.

Built as a fast static site in Astro with plain TypeScript, Averleigh loads quickly on a phone, keeps motion quiet and respects reduced-motion settings. The visiting, membership, lesson and contact forms are built in.

summary.en: Ardor is a complete website for an independent marketing agency in Amsterdam. It is built around one idea: campaigns people talk about, then remember. The home

brief.en: Make an agency site that feels like the work it sells: bold, photographic and quick to read, while keeping the four services, the cases and the brief form easy to find.

approach.en: One red-lit portrait opens the site, set under a heavy grotesk and a mono meta layer, with dark and light themes and every case written as brief, idea, execution and result.

outcome.en: A complete six-page agency site with a case study template, a journal with posts and a brief form, ready to start a conversation from the first screen.

about.en:
Ardor is a complete website for an independent marketing agency in Amsterdam. It is built around one idea: campaigns people talk about, then remember.

The home page opens on a red-lit portrait under the line Made to be felt, then shows the four ways in, a featured case that leads with the nine days it took to sell out, how a brief becomes a campaign in ten weeks, a client voice, seven long partnerships, the 42 people on the floor and the latest notes from the journal.

Behind it sit a work page with every case and its lead figure, a case study template that runs from the brief to the result, a services page with a price and a timeline for each service, an agency page that tells the story year by year, a journal with filters and a contents rail on every post, and a brief form that reads like a conversation.

The type is Inter Tight for headlines and text, with Geist Mono for the details. The palette is near black, red and ember, with a cream light theme on request, and the imagery is red-lit portrait photography. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis.

summary.en: Tarn is a complete website for a cash-flow forecasting product for small and mid-size businesses. It is built around one question: how long will your cash last?

brief.en: Cash software usually reads like accounting. The brief: explain what the product does on the first screen, show the forecast itself instead of describing it, keep pricing plain and make starting a trial feel safe.

approach.en: We built it light and calm: near-white paper, ink and one moss green, Urbanist for headlines and Geist for text, with real product screens framed by dark basalt and moss photography. Motion stays quiet and every section answers one question an owner asks. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis.

outcome.en: A site that shows the product before it explains it: a working-looking dashboard on the first screen, a scenario planner, an eighteen-month forecast, plain per-business pricing and a 14-day trial with no card, one click from every page.

about.en:
The home page opens on that line over a working dashboard framed by moss-covered stone, then shows what the forecast reads from, lets an owner test a hire or a lost client before it happens, walks through setting up in an afternoon and lists the pricing by business, not by person.

Behind it sit a product page with the weekly cash flow, scenarios and a bills calendar, customer stories, plans from $39 a month, a journal, the story of the team, a security page and a booking page for a 20-minute walkthrough.

The type is Urbanist for headlines and Geist for text. The palette is ink, paper and moss green, and the imagery is basalt and moss photography. Built with Astro, GSAP and Lenis.

summary.en: Amble is a complete online store for everyday sneakers, runners and trail shoes, designed in Portland and made in two family factories in Elche, Spain. It is bu

brief.en: Make a shoe store feel friendly and clean while 75 styles share one grid, one studio grey and one accent colour.

approach.en: Put every shoe on the same studio grey, keep tomato as the one accent, and let the hero step each shoe in and out.

outcome.en: A complete store with catalogue, size tool, bag, checkout and accounts, also built as a Shopify theme.

about.en:
Amble is a complete online store for everyday sneakers, runners and trail shoes, designed in Portland and made in two family factories in Elche, Spain. It is built around one idea: the shoe carries all the colour. The page is paper white, every product sits on the same light studio grey, and one tomato heel tab runs through every shoe, photo and the logo dot.

The home page opens on a full-screen hero that steps through five shoes, with colourway chips, a size picker and Add to bag. A statement follows, Step into the city in shoes made for long walks, easy runs and dry trails, then New arrivals, Explore our collection (Everyday, Running, Trail) and a lifestyle strip titled Built for miles, worn all day, which holds a Tempo feature: go long, stay light, with its rocker sole, 40 mm of foam and 255 g weight. Comfort you can feel explains the Daily's knit upper, heel cushion and wave-cut sole beside a spec panel with weight, heel stack, drop and a colour selector. Best sellers, a promise ticker, four customer notes, Made in Elche, Spain with its two factories and $45 resole, a service strip and a newsletter close the page.

Behind it sit the full shop: 75 styles across Everyday, Court, Slip-ons, Running, Trail, Sandals, Boots and Kids, with filters and sort, product pages with a gallery per colourway, a size picker and customer reviews, a Find your size tool, Our factories, Help, a wishlist, a bag drawer, checkout and customer accounts with orders and addresses.

The type is Bricolage Grotesque for headlines and Instrument Sans for text. The palette is paper white, studio grey and ink, with tomato as the only accent. Built with Astro and Lenis, and packaged as a Shopify theme named Plinth.

summary.en: Lasada Pippen is a complete keynote speaker and communication coaching website solution built to position communication as a competitive advantage across corpor

brief.en: A keynote speaker and communication coach needed a site that does what a speaker reel cannot: hold attention in silence. The brief asked for editorial confidence — a place where event organisers can gauge stage presence, and coaching clients can feel the clarity being sold — without the site ever talking over its subject.

approach.en: We designed an editorial layout in Wix Studio that treats Lasada like a publication cover: large portrait photography, generous whitespace, and typography that carries authority on its own. Booking is wired directly into the site so an enquiry becomes a scheduled conversation in one motion, and the blog gives the coaching practice a voice between engagements.

outcome.en: The site now works as the pitch that precedes the pitch — organisers see composure and polish before they ever watch a reel. Speaking, coaching, and writing each have a clear path, and the booking flow removes the email back-and-forth that used to sit between interest and a confirmed call.

about.en:
Lasada Pippen is a complete keynote speaker and communication coaching website solution built to position communication as a competitive advantage across corporate, educational, and leadership environments. The project was designed with a strong focus on editorial storytelling, cinematic presentation, and structured user flow, creating a premium digital platform that reflects clarity, confidence, and leadership.

The website includes dedicated experiences for Corporate Speaking, Educational Speaking, Coaching, Blog, and Booking, each organized to guide visitors through keynote programs, coaching pathways, communication frameworks, and inquiry flows with clear hierarchy and intuitive navigation. Structured content sections and conversion-focused layouts help visitors quickly understand offerings, audience fit, and outcomes.

The visual direction combines oversized typography, cinematic imagery, dark contrast sections, and minimalist layouts to create a modern and immersive brand experience. Editorial spacing, framework-driven sections, and layered visual compositions reinforce the premium positioning while maintaining strong readability and consistency across pages.

Built in Wix Studio with responsiveness and scalability in mind, the platform supports future content expansion, speaking updates, blog publishing, and coaching growth. The result is a refined and future-ready digital presence designed for a modern keynote speaker and communication brand.

summary.en: Orvel is a complete website for an independent brand and digital studio in London and Lisbon, founded in 2013, with thirty-four designers, writers, strategists

brief.en: An independent brand and digital studio wanted a site that behaves like its work. Founders and marketing teams needed to see real projects, what the studio makes, who is on the floor in two cities and how to start, without the usual wall of agency adjectives or a template that could belong to anyone.

approach.en: Let the work lead and keep the page quiet. The hero is a close-up portrait that responds like liquid under the pointer, the studio reel opens out of the statement, and sixteen projects sit in a pinned deck with each client name set in its own typeface. Services turn on a capability drum, the journal is a magazine that turns its pages, and the two cities share one split scene with live clocks.

outcome.en: A visitor can play the reel, move through the sixteen projects, read the studio journal, see both offices in real time and start a project from a short brief in a few minutes. Pages stay quick on a phone, motion respects reduced-motion settings, and every project and note is a content file the studio edits without touching the design.

about.en:
The site includes Home, Work with sixteen project pages, Services, Studio, Journal with thirty notes, and Contact, plus Privacy and 404 pages.

The visual direction is a light editorial page that turns dark only where it helps, with a wide grotesk for display and a monospace for labels. The hero is a close-up portrait that moves like liquid under the pointer, the studio reel opens out of the opening statement, each client name is set in its own typeface in a pinned project deck, services turn on a capability drum, and the journal is a magazine that turns its pages as you scroll.

Built as a fast static site in Astro with plain TypeScript, GSAP, Lenis and WebGL, Orvel keeps its projects and journal notes as content files, respects reduced-motion settings and works on a phone. The studio reel, the two-city scene with live clocks and the project brief form are built in.

summary.en: 4 Dolfins is a complete film and television portfolio website solution built to showcase productions, formats, and media recognition in a bold and cinematic dig

brief.en: A film and television production company needed its portfolio to feel like its medium. Static thumbnails flatten cinematic work, but autoplaying showreels bury it. 4Dolfins needed a site that could present formats, films, and series with the pacing of a title sequence — and stay fast while doing it.

approach.en: We leaned into darkness: a near-black canvas where stills and key art provide all the light, with motion used the way an editor uses a cut — sparingly, and always on purpose. The catalogue runs on a CMS so every new production slots into the same considered frame the moment it wraps.

outcome.en: The portfolio now screens rather than lists. Each project gets a presentation worthy of a premiere, commissioners can move from format to format without friction, and the company adds new work in minutes instead of redesign cycles.

about.en:
4 Dolfins is a complete film and television portfolio website solution built to showcase productions, formats, and media recognition in a bold and cinematic digital environment. The project was designed with a strong focus on visual impact, structured storytelling, and content clarity, creating a platform that reflects the scale and credibility of the brand.

The website includes essential sections such as About, Formats, Film, TV, TV Personality, and Media, each organized to guide visitors through projects, achievements, and press coverage with clear hierarchy and smooth navigation. Content blocks and media cards help present shows, formats, awards, and articles in an easy-to-browse layout.

The visual direction uses dark themes, high-contrast typography, and large imagery to create an immersive entertainment-focused experience. Structured grids, featured highlights, and modular sections allow each production and media mention to stand out while keeping the design consistent.

Built with responsiveness and scalability in mind, the site supports continuous expansion as new projects and media features are added. The result is a strong, future-ready digital presence suited for production houses and media brands that need a premium and authoritative online showcase.

content.label: How do I get started with Relyon Dev?
content.text: Simply fill out the contact form, and we’ll reach out through email or WhatsApp based on your preferred method of communication.

content.label: How involved do I need to be during the project?
content.text: You only need to share your content, preferences, and feedback at important stages. We handle the complete design, development, testing, and launch process.

content.label: How long does it take to build a website?
content.text: Most websites are completed within 2–6 weeks, depending on the number of pages, design direction, and required features.

content.label: Do you provide support after the website is launched?
content.text: Yes. We offer post-launch maintenance, content updates, and technical support to ensure your website continues to perform well.

content.label: Do you create responsive and eCommerce websites?
content.text: Absolutely. Every site we build is fully responsive, and we also develop complete eCommerce stores with payment integration and custom product layouts.

content.label: Do you work with international clients?
content.text: Yes — most of our work is international. Relyon Dev serves clients across the United States, United Kingdom, Europe, the Middle East and worldwide, working across time zones with updates over email or WhatsApp.
